subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should systemd-managed Gateway turns continue to treat literal config `env.KIMI_API_KEY` as supported durable runtime auth for Kimi Coding, or should durable daemon auth be steered to `.env`/auth profiles with status/docs changes?
rationale: The code already has a config-env runtime path, but the generated service environment intentionally does not inline those secrets and the reporter's release already contained the older config-env application behavior.

options.title: Keep config env supported
options.body: Preserve the documented config-env path and add focused systemd/Kimi runtime proof plus status wording that reflects the actual Gateway credential context.

options.title: Prefer durable auth profiles
options.body: Update docs/status/onboarding to make per-agent auth profiles or global `.env` the recommended daemon-safe path and warn when config env is CLI-only or ambiguous.

options.title: Require explicit migration/doctor repair
options.body: Add a doctor or startup recovery path that converts or flags unsupported daemon credential sources before agent turns fail over.

recommendation.title: Keep config env supported
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented config-env path and add focused systemd/Kimi runtime proof plus status wording that reflects the actual Gateway credential context.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-surface history on config IO, service-env planning, docs, and model-status behavior.
